title: record
description: Client -> robot. Legacy recording verbs remain available. L3 app review is opt-in: episode_start with review_required:true -> episode_stop -> episode_keep OR episode_reject (both require the stable episode_id) -> session_end. Check review_supported via review_status before starting. An awaiting-review episode is excluded from backend registration and upload, including across restarts. Keep releases it; Reject deletes only that episode. A review_status lists the authenticated operator's pending episodes and restores their active review capture. No operator identity is accepted from the client. New clients use request_id, echoed in the reply: retry the SAME ID for the SAME operation. Capture and review use independent serialization lanes for both correlated and legacy clients, so review never blocks Stop. The gateway caches 128 successful replies per connection, not refusals/errors. Service calls time out after 5 seconds; recover status after an uncertain timeout before another mutation, especially Start. Reject acknowledges durable quarantine; background cleanup reclaims the payload. Completed decision receipts have a 30-day replay window; incomplete decisions do not expire. Review takes require explicit decisions and have configurable held-storage limits. After reconnect, query review_status and retry the durable Keep/Reject decision by episode ID. Legacy replies without request_id cannot be correlated and must not complete a new request. L2 does not implement this review extension. Legacy session_discard/discard/discard_last differ by stack: L2 destroys data, L3 closes collection bookkeeping without deletion. Never use those aliases for episode review. Legacy stop differs by stack: on L2 it ends the session as well as the episode; on L3 it finalizes only the episode. Client-supplied nori:review-required tags are reserved and ignored; only review_required:true on episode_start opts into review.

action.description: L3: episode_start starts capture. Without review_required, episode_stop finalizes and retains the take for upload. With review_required, it holds the stopped take for an explicit episode_keep or episode_reject. episode_discard finalizes the ACTIVE take with a retained DISCARDED outcome on L3; it is not post-stop deletion. session_start/end manage collection bookkeeping and never release a review hold. review_status lists pending episodes for the authenticated operator. L2 legacy behavior is unchanged: episode_discard destroys an episode and session_discard destroys the session. Prefer explicit review verbs on supporting L3 robots. Legacy start opens both a session and an episode. Legacy stop ends the entire session on L2, but only finalizes the episode on L3. On L2, discard aliases session_discard and discard_last targets the most recent session; on L3 both only close collection bookkeeping. Do not replace episode_reject with any legacy discard alias.

task.description: Free-text task label recorded with the episode. Meaningful only on the verbs that OPEN something (session_start, episode_start, legacy start); ignored elsewhere.

request_id.description: Correlation and replay key; reuse only for retries of the identical request.

review_required.description: episode_start opt-in; persists the review hold before capture begins. Requires review_supported.

episode_id.description: Stable ID returned by episode_start/episode_stop, required for episode_keep/episode_reject.

tags.description: episode_start only: labels stored with the episode. They can select recorder behaviour ("aspire" = the long action-silence window for agent takes). The nori:review-required label is reserved for gateway-to-recorder control. The L3 gateway removes client-supplied copies and inserts it only for an explicit review_required:true request; other labels retain their existing behavior.

outcome.description: episode_stop only. Omitted = success (a human stop). An unknown value is refused with record_status ok:false, never stored as success.

notes.description: episode_stop (including legacy stop) only: free text stored with the episode. Ignored by episode_discard, preserving legacy behavior.
